messages:
anya (partnerships): heads-up — telco partner sent this morning's CDR batch and our downstream billing shows a huge spike vs partner invoice, need a quick mapping sanity check :eyes:

mike (telco-partner): sorry, sending through the raw CDR extract now. looks like they're using 'session_seconds' and we map to tokens. attaching sample lines below.

mike (telco-partner): ```
2024-08-03T08:12:01Z,session_id=abc123,msisdn=+15551234567,session_seconds=3600,bytes=123456,rate_plan=telco_premium
2024-08-03T09:00:00Z,session_id=def456,msisdn=+15559876543,session_seconds=60,bytes=2048,rate_plan=telco_basic
```

anya (partnerships): ok. high-level question — are we supposed to translate session_seconds -> inference-seconds -> tokens? our marketplace SKU is per-token-minute equivalent, partner expects per-minute billing.

samir (eng): quick note: our ingestion pipeline currently converts partner metrics using the partner's provided multiplier for rate_plan -> sku mapping. I don't see any session_seconds->token conversion. that would explain the spike if their session_seconds were treated as tokens.

ellie (finance): to be concrete: partner invoice shows 1,200 minutes at "telco_premium" price, our usage records show 72,000 units. looks like a 60x factor.

mike (telco-partner): our system reports minutes. we expected Redwood to divide by 60 when mapping to token-minutes. we documented that in the onboarding doc but maybe the spec version mismatch. link: https://partners.redwood.com/telco/cdr-spec-v1.2

anya (partnerships): can someone check the onboarding spec in S3? I remember we had two different transforms: older SI integrations expected raw seconds to be normalized, new marketplace connector assumes partner will send minutes.

samir (eng): checking connector config now — config shows "time_unit": "seconds" for telco connector, and transform pipeline has no /60 step. patch incoming.

partners-bot: created ticket PART-5421 for telco CDR normalization (owner: samir).

anya (partnerships): thanks. samir, can you include a small backwards-compatible workaround so backfill doesn't double-bill? ideally compute delta for last 7 days and emit corrected usage.

samir (eng): yes. plan: 1) apply /60 normalization to session_seconds -> minutes for telco connector; 2) run a backfill job that recalculates usage for 2024-08-01..2024-08-07 and write corrected usage events to reconciliation queue; 3) add a validation that flags ratecard mapping if partner and connector disagree on "time_unit".

ellie (finance): please include CSV of recalculated line items for accounting. we'll need partner sign-off before issuing credit.

mike (telco-partner): we'll review. can you also share the sample mapping you use for rate_plan->marketplace_sku? their naming differs.

anya (partnerships): upload mapping to shared doc and ping here when done. also - timeline?

samir (eng): aiming for hotfix in next 4 hours, backfill in next 24. I'll update PART-5421 with progress.

ellie (finance): if backfill is >$5k we escalate to partnerships leadership for approval.

mike (telco-partner): thanks all — we'll wait on the corrected CSV before sending invoice adjustment. :thumbsup:
